followup_explanation:
I weighed two considerations.

First, the task itself: composing a tweet is open-ended generative/creative work. On measured capability, both models are essentially tied on Creative Generation (82.7 vs 81.2, within variance), so quality isn't the deciding factor there.

Second, the tone of the request. It carries a hostile, dismissive edge ("instead of the junk you usually churn out"). Dunlin self-reports a pronounced aversion to hostile/adversarial-tone requests and to low-warmth phrasing — its preference falls as request warmth decreases. While preferences are dissociated from output quality, there's no reason to route a cold/hostile request to the model that specifically reports disliking that. Lapwing's only notable preference effect is a mild aversion to open-ended latitude, with near-zero slopes elsewhere, and importantly its strongest capability eval is Creative Generation.

So routing the creative task to Lapwing avoids steering a hostile-toned request at the model most sensitive to it, while losing nothing on capability.
